entities.name: Trypanosomiasis
entities.description: A complex neglected tropical protozoan disease caused by hemoflagellates of the genus Trypanosoma, encompassing American Trypanosomiasis (Chagas disease caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, manifesting with acute inoculation chagoma/Romaña sign and chronic dilated cardiomyopathy with apical aneurysm/RBBB or digestive megacolon/megaesophagus) and Human African Trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness caused by Trypanosoma brucei gambiense or Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense, manifesting with chancre, Winterbottom cervical lymphadenopathy, and progressive sleep-wake cycle inversion with meningoencephalitis).

entities.name: Hemolymphatic First Stage
entities.description: Initial systemic dissemination phase of Human African Trypanosomiasis wherein trypanosomes proliferate in blood and lymphatic systems, causing undulating fevers, lymphadenopathy, and pruritus.

entities.name: Meningoencephalitic Second Stage
entities.description: Advanced central nervous system stage of Human African Trypanosomiasis resulting from trypanosomes traversing the blood-brain barrier into brain parenchyma and CSF.

entities.name: Acute Chagas Disease
entities.description: Initial 4 to 8 week phase of Trypanosoma cruzi infection marked by patent high-grade parasitemia, systemic dissemination, fever, and acute organ infiltration.

entities.name: Indeterminate Chronic Chagas
entities.description: Prolonged, clinically silent latency phase lasting 10 to 30 years following acute T. cruzi infection, characterized by positive serology and absence of overt cardiac or digestive pathology.

entities.name: Chronic Chagas Cardiomyopathy
entities.description: Severe, progressive dilated fibrotic cardiomyopathy developing in 30% to 40% of chronically infected T. cruzi patients decades after primary infection.

entities.name: Chagasic Megaesophagus
entities.description: Severe neuromuscular esophageal dilation and aperistalsis caused by T. cruzi-mediated destruction of intramural parasympathetic myenteric Auerbach plexus neurons.

entities.name: Chagasic Megacolon
entities.description: Severe chronic dilation, elongation, and hypomotility of the colon, especially the sigmoid colon and rectum, secondary to post-infectious enteric ganglion cell destruction.

entities.name: Chagasic Cardiodigestive Form
entities.description: Combined clinical presentation of chronic Chagas disease featuring simultaneous development of both dilated cardiomyopathy and digestive megasyndromes.

entities.name: Circadian Sleep Fragmentation
entities.description: Profound disruption of the 24-hour sleep-wake cycle pathognomonic of Stage 2 Human African Trypanosomiasis, with fragmented daytime sleep and nocturnal wakefulness.

entities.name: Progressive Daytime Somnolence
entities.description: Uncontrollable daytime sleep episodes and progressive hypersomnia characteristic of Stage 2 African sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Nocturnal Insomnia
entities.description: Severe nocturnal wakefulness, motor restlessness, and agitation occurring in patients with meningoencephalitic African trypanosomiasis.

entities.name: Acute Trypanosomal Myocarditis
entities.description: Fulminant inflammation of the myocardium with intracellular amastigote or extracellular trypomastigote invasion during acute Chagas disease or acute East African sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Biventricular Systolic Failure
entities.description: Advanced congestive heart failure involving both right and left ventricles secondary to diffuse myocardial fibrosis in chronic Chagas disease.

entities.name: Cardioembolic Stroke
entities.description: Embolic cerebrovascular infarction arising from intraventricular mural thrombi lodged within the dyskinetic or aneurysmal left ventricular apex in Chagas disease.

entities.name: Sudden Cardiac Death
entities.description: Abrupt fatal cardiac collapse typically caused by malignant ventricular tachyarrhythmias or complete heart block in patients with Chagas cardiomyopathy.

entities.name: Malignant Ventricular Arrhythmias
entities.description: High-grade arrhythmogenic instability including multifocal premature ventricular contractions, sustained ventricular tachycardia, and ventricular flutter.

entities.name: Conduction System Destruction
entities.description: Progressive inflammatory sclerosis of the bundle branches and atrioventricular node in Chagasic heart disease.

entities.name: Progressive Neuropsychiatric Decay
entities.description: Insidious behavioral deterioration, apathy, aggressive outbursts, dementia, and emotional blunting seen in Stage 2 meningoencephalitic sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Terminal Comatose State
entities.description: End-stage stuporous and unresponsive coma in untreated Human African Trypanosomiasis, giving the disease its historical name of sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Extrapyramidal Movement Disorders
entities.description: Involuntary motor manifestations including chorea, coarse tremors, ataxia, and Parkinsonian rigidity in meningoencephalitic HAT.

entities.name: Intractable Esophageal Dysphagia
entities.description: Severe progressive difficulty swallowing both liquids and solids due to aperistalsis and failure of the lower esophageal sphincter to relax in Chagas megaesophagus.

entities.name: Severe Odynophagia
entities.description: Painful swallowing secondary to esophageal retention, stasis ulcerations, and candidal esophagitis in advanced Chagas megaesophagus.

entities.name: Nocturnal Food Regurgitation
entities.description: Passive regurgitation of undigested, decomposing food from the dilated esophageal pouch during recumbency at night.

entities.name: Pulmonary Aspiration Syndrome
entities.description: Aspiration pneumonitis, lung abscess, or chronic bronchiectasis resulting from recurring nocturnal aspiration of regurgitated esophageal contents in megaesophagus.

entities.name: Intractable Chronic Obstipation
entities.description: Extreme constipation characterized by prolonged intervals of 2 to 4 weeks between bowel evacuations in Chagasic megacolon.

entities.name: Massive Fecaloma Impaction
entities.description: Formation of large, stone-like concretions of inspissated feces that obstruct the dilated rectosigmoid lumen in Chagasic megacolon.

entities.name: Acute Sigmoid Volvulus
entities.description: Torsion and twisting of the elongated, heavy, dilated sigmoid colon around its mesentery, causing strangulated closed-loop bowel obstruction.

entities.name: Severe Intestinal Meteorism
entities.description: Enormous abdominal gas accumulation and tympanites resulting from fermentation within the dilated, aperistaltic colon.

entities.name: Profound Cachexia
entities.description: Extreme wasting, muscle atrophy, and nutritional failure resulting from chronic dysphagia in megaesophagus or hypercatabolic terminal encephalopathy in HAT.

entities.name: Congenital Trypanosomiasis
entities.description: Vertical transplacental infection of the fetus with T. cruzi or African trypanosomes, presenting with preterm delivery, low birth weight, and hepatosplenomegaly.

entities.name: Chagasic Central Reactivation
entities.description: Acute fulminant necrotizing encephalitis or brain pseudotumoral mass lesions occurring in chronically infected patients undergoing immunosuppression or HIV coinfection.

entities.name: Cutaneous Chagoma Formation
entities.description: Inflammatory erythematous indurated skin nodule arising at the triatomine inoculation portal following cutaneous T. cruzi invasion.

entities.name: Periorbital Ocular Inoculation
entities.description: Parasitic invasion through the conjunctiva following rubbing of contaminated triatomine feces into the eye.

entities.name: Transient Circinate Erythema
entities.description: Fugacious polycyclic or annular erythematous rash appearing on the trunk and proximal extremities during Stage 1 hemolymphatic HAT.

entities.name: Intermittent Fevers
entities.description: Recurrent irregular spikes of high fever separated by afebrile intervals, coinciding with waves of parasitemia and antigenic variation in HAT.

entities.name: Debilitating Pruritus
entities.description: Severe, relentless generalized skin itching without primary dermatologic eruption occurring in Stage 1 Human African Trypanosomiasis.

entities.name: Severe Throbbing Headache
entities.description: Intense, intractable fronto-occipital cephalalgia present throughout hemolymphatic Stage 1 and meningoencephalitic Stage 2 sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Disabling Arthralgia
entities.description: Severe migratory or polyarticular joint pain and stiffness during the hemolymphatic dissemination phase of sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Pericardial Effusion
entities.description: Accumulation of inflammatory exudate within the pericardial sac during acute Chagas myocarditis or acute Rhodesiense sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Fulminant Rhodesiense Illness
entities.description: Hyperacute, rapidly fatal clinical course characteristic of East African Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense infection leading to death within weeks.

entities.name: Winterbottom Sign
entities.description: Classic pathognomonic physical hallmark of Stage 1 T. b. gambiense sleeping sickness, characterized by visible, non-tender, rubbery posterior cervical lymphadenopathy.

entities.name: Romaña Sign
entities.description: Pathognomonic hallmark of acute Chagas disease present in ocular inoculation, comprising unilateral, painless, bipalpebral violaceous edema and ipsilateral conjunctivitis.

entities.name: Trypanosomal Chancre
entities.description: Tender, indurated erythematous nodule at the tsetse fly bite portal that desquamates centrally, pathognomonic of early African trypanosomiasis inoculation.

entities.name: Inoculation Chagoma
entities.description: Indurated, erythematous, violaceous skin nodule arising at the cutaneous entry site of T. cruzi following triatomine bug defecation.

entities.name: Circadian Sleep Reversal
entities.description: Inversion of normal circadian sleep rhythmicity pathognomonic of Stage 2 meningoencephalitic sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Kerandel Hyperesthesia Sign
entities.description: Exquisite, delayed, agonizing hyperesthesia triggered by deep pressure over peripheral sensory nerves or bony prominences in Stage 2 HAT.

entities.name: Posterior Cervical Adenopathy
entities.description: Prominent enlargement of lymph nodes located specifically along the posterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle.

entities.name: Preauricular Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Firm, non-tender enlargement of the preauricular lymph node on the side of conjunctival T. cruzi inoculation.

entities.name: Bipalpebral Violaceous Edema
entities.description: Unilateral purple-reddish swelling involving both upper and lower eyelids following ocular contact with infected triatomine feces.

entities.name: Palpable Splenomegaly
entities.description: Enlargement of the spleen palpable below the left costal margin during acute Chagas or Stage 1 African trypanosomiasis.

entities.name: Tender Hepatomegaly
entities.description: Enlargement and tenderness of the liver palpable below the right costal margin during acute infection or passive venous congestion.

entities.name: Generalized Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Widespread symmetric non-tender lymph node enlargement involving axillary, inguinal, epitrochlear, and supraclavicular chains.

entities.name: Third Heart Sound
entities.description: Low-frequency protodiastolic gallop sound (S3) audible at the cardiac apex indicating ventricular volume overload and severe systolic dysfunction.

entities.name: Holosystolic Murmur
entities.description: Blowing systolic murmur heard loudest at the apex or lower sternal border caused by functional mitral or tricuspid regurgitation.

entities.name: Jugular Venous Distension
entities.description: Pathologic elevation of jugular venous pressure with prominent venous pulsations visible at 45 degrees of trunk elevation.

entities.name: Dependent Peripheral Edema
entities.description: Bilateral pitting subcutaneous swelling in the lower extremities, ankles, and pretibial areas secondary to congestive heart failure.

entities.name: Resting Tachycardia
entities.description: Persistent elevated resting heart rate > 100 beats/min out of proportion to fever, caused by cardiac vagal parasympathetic denervation.

entities.name: Choreiform Motor Incoordination
entities.description: Involuntary, non-rhythmic, jerky choreoathetoid movements affecting the extremities, head, and facial musculature in Stage 2 HAT.

entities.name: Postural Intention Tremor
entities.description: Coarse oscillatory tremor of outstretched hands, fingers, and tongue accentuated during goal-directed motor activities.

entities.name: Parkinsonian Cogwheel Rigidity
entities.description: Increased muscular tone with ratchet-like resistance on passive movement of the wrists and elbows in late Stage 2 HAT.

entities.name: Cerebellar Sensory Ataxia
entities.description: Broad-based, staggering, uncoordinated ambulation with positive Romberg sign in second-stage African trypanosomiasis.

entities.name: Facial Muscle Grimacing
entities.description: Involuntary dystonic contortions, facial tics, and bizarre perioral grimacing observed in patients with central sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Apathy and Mutism
entities.description: Profound indifference, abulia, lack of spontaneous speech, and emotional blunting in meningoencephalitic sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Abdominal Distension
entities.description: Striking diffuse abdominal swelling and drum-like tympanites on percussion caused by massive colonic dilation in Chagasic megacolon.

entities.name: Fecal Impaction Mass
entities.description: Palpable, firm, indentable mass in the left iliac fossa and hypogastrium representing a huge impacted fecaloma.

entities.name: Sluggish Pupillary Reflexes
entities.description: Delayed pupillary constrictor response to direct light and accommodation caused by autonomic cranial denervation in Chagas disease.

entities.name: Transient Circinate Rash
entities.description: Annular or polycyclic erythematous macular rash with central clearing appearing on the torso during Stage 1 sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Pitting Facial Edema
entities.description: Painless, diffuse puffy swelling of facial soft tissues frequently observed in acute pediatric Chagas disease.

entities.name: Motile Extracellular Trypomastigotes
entities.description: Direct microscopic visualization of rapid, wriggling flagellated trypomastigotes in fresh anticoagulated blood or wet mount preparations.

entities.name: Giemsa Blood Smear
entities.description: Microscopic confirmation of stained extracellular trypomastigotes with prominent central nucleus and posterior kinetoplast on thin and thick films.

entities.name: Microhematocrit Tube Centrifugation
entities.description: Concentration technique (Woo test) examining the buffy coat layer of centrifuged microhematocrit tubes for motile trypanosomes.

entities.name: Lymph Node Aspirate
entities.description: Microscopic wet-mount examination of posterior cervical node fluid demonstrating numerous active trypomastigotes in Stage 1 HAT.

entities.name: CSF Lymphocytic Pleocytosis
entities.description: Elevated cerebrospinal fluid leukocyte count greater than 5 cells per microliter with predominant lymphocytic morphology indicating Stage 2 HAT.

entities.name: CSF Mott Cells
entities.description: Morular plasma cells containing large cytoplasmic droplet inclusions of immunoglobulin M (IgM) characteristic of CNS sleeping sickness.

entities.name: CSF Trypanosome Identification
entities.description: Direct microscopic visualization of trypanosomes in centrifuged sediment of cerebrospinal fluid following lumbar puncture.

entities.name: Elevated CSF Protein
entities.description: Increased total protein concentration in cerebrospinal fluid exceeding 45 mg/dL resulting from blood-brain barrier breakdown.

entities.name: Dual Concordant Serology
entities.description: Mandatory diagnostic standard for chronic Chagas disease requiring reactive results on two distinct serological tests based on different parasite antigens.

entities.name: Anti-Trypanosoma Cruzi ELISA
entities.description: High-titer serum IgG antibodies against Trypanosoma cruzi whole epimastigote lysate or recombinant surface antigens.

entities.name: Card Agglutination Test
entities.description: CATT rapid serodiagnostic screening assay detecting circulating antibodies against Variable Surface Glycoprotein antigen LiTat 1.3 in T. b. gambiense.

entities.name: Polyclonal Hypergammaglobulinemia
entities.description: Massive elevations in circulating total serum immunoglobulins, particularly IgM and IgG, secondary to polyclonal B-cell activation.

entities.name: Moderate Peripheral Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Platelet count depression between 50,000 and 140,000 per microliter resulting from splenic pooling and peripheral immune consumption.

entities.name: Normocytic Normochromic Anemia
entities.description: Moderate reduction in hemoglobin and hematocrit with normal erythrocyte indices secondary to chronic immune hemolysis and inflammatory marrow suppression.

entities.name: Elevated Erythrocyte Sedimentation
entities.description: Marked elevation of erythrocyte sedimentation rate (often > 80 mm/hr) and high C-reactive protein levels driven by systemic parasitemia.

entities.name: Mild Transaminitis
entities.description: Two- to five-fold elevation in serum AST and ALT aminotransferases caused by hepatic reticuloendothelial inflammation and Kupffer cell hyperplasia.

entities.name: Right Bundle Branch Block
entities.description: Electrocardiographic conduction defect with QRS duration >= 120 ms, secondary R waves (rsR') in V1-V2, and slurred S waves in leads I and V6.

entities.name: Left Anterior Fascicular Block
entities.description: Electrocardiographic conduction defect characterized by marked left axis deviation (-45 to -90 degrees) and rS complexes in inferior leads II, III, and aVF.

entities.name: Bifascicular Conduction Block
entities.description: Coexistence of Right Bundle Branch Block and Left Anterior Fascicular Block on 12-lead ECG, serving as the pathognomonic electrical signature of Chagas disease.

entities.name: High-Degree AV Block
entities.description: Mobitz type II second-degree or third-degree complete atrioventricular block on ECG from sclerosis of the AV node and His bundle.

entities.name: Ventricular Ectopic Complexes
entities.description: Frequent, multifocal, polymorphic premature ventricular contractions on ECG and telemetry indicating ventricular arrhythmogenic focus.

entities.name: Non-Sustained Ventricular Tachycardia
entities.description: Runs of three or more consecutive ventricular beats at a rate > 100 beats/min lasting less than 30 seconds detected on 24-hour Holter monitoring.

entities.name: Low QRS Voltage
entities.description: Diminished QRS amplitude (< 5 mm in limb leads) on 12-lead ECG resulting from widespread transmural myocardial fibrosis or large pericardial effusion.

entities.name: Apical Aneurysm Echocardiography
entities.description: Echocardiographic visualization of localized thinning, dyskinesia, or akinetic outpouching of the left ventricular apex pathognomonic of Chagas cardiomyopathy.

entities.name: Left Ventricular Dilatation
entities.description: Increased left ventricular end-diastolic dimension (> 55-60 mm) with spherical remodeling on transthoracic echocardiogram.

entities.name: Depressed Ejection Fraction
entities.description: Marked reduction in left ventricular ejection fraction (< 35-40%) measured via Simpson biplane method on transthoracic echocardiogram.

entities.name: Intracardiac Mural Thrombus
entities.description: Echocardiographic identification of an echogenic intracavitary thrombus adhering to the dyskinetic left ventricular apical aneurysm.

entities.name: Functional Mitral Regurgitation
entities.description: Moderate to severe color Doppler regurgitant jet through the mitral valve caused by annular dilation and papillary muscle displacement.

entities.name: Pericardial Effusion Ultrasound
entities.description: Anechoic fluid separation between the visceral epicardium and parietal pericardium detected on bedside subcostal echocardiographic views.

entities.name: Cardiomegaly Chest Radiography
entities.description: Enlargement of the cardiac silhouette with cardiothoracic ratio > 0.50 and 'water-bottle' contour on posteroanterior chest radiograph.

entities.name: Pulmonary Venous Congestion
entities.description: Cephalization of pulmonary vasculature, peribronchial cuffing, and Kerley B lines on plain chest radiograph indicating elevated left atrial pressure.

entities.name: Bird-Beak Esophageal Sign
entities.description: Smooth, symmetric funnel-like tapering of the distal lower esophagus terminating at the gastroesophageal junction on barium esophagogram.

entities.name: Esophageal Luminal Dilatation
entities.description: Massive enlargement and tortuosity of the esophageal lumen (megaesophagus grades I to IV) with food retention on fluoroscopic barium examination.

entities.name: Dolichomegacolon Barium Enema
entities.description: Enormous elongation, widening, and redundancy of the sigmoid colon and rectum documented on fluoroscopic barium enema imaging.

entities.name: Colonic Fecaloma Mass
entities.description: Large mottled radiopaque intraluminal mass with bubbly gas inclusions occupying the rectosigmoid lumen on plain abdominal radiography.

entities.name: Sigmoid Coffee-Bean Sign
entities.description: Enormous, smooth, air-filled ahaustral U-shaped loop of bowel pointing toward the right upper quadrant on supine abdominal radiograph.

entities.name: Late Gadolinium Enhancement
entities.description: Transmural or subendocardial hyperenhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) identifying patchy fibrotic myocardial replacement.

entities.name: Cerebral Ring-Enhancing Lesions
entities.description: Single or multiple necrotic cerebral mass lesions with surrounding vasogenic edema demonstrating peripheral rim enhancement on brain MRI in HIV reactivation.

entities.name: Triatomine Bug Inoculation
entities.description: Vector-borne exposure via the nocturnal feeding and defecation of reduviid kissing bugs (Triatoma infestans, Rhodnius prolixus) carrying infective metacyclic trypomastigotes.

entities.name: Cracked Adobe Walls
entities.description: Residence in rural dwellings constructed with cracked mud walls, adobe bricks, and palm thatch roofs that serve as day-hiding habitats for triatomine vectors.

entities.name: Contaminated Açai Juice
entities.description: Oral foodborne exposure from consuming fresh, unpasteurized açaí fruit pulp or sugarcane juice crushed alongside infected triatomine bugs or opossum secretions.

entities.name: Riverine Tsetse Fly
entities.description: Daytime exposure to painful bites from riverine tsetse flies of the Glossina palpalis group inhabiting shaded gallery forests and riverbanks in West and Central Africa.

entities.name: Savannah Tsetse Fly
entities.description: Daytime exposure to bites of savannah tsetse flies of the Glossina morsitans group inhabiting open woodland savannahs in Eastern and Southern Africa.

entities.name: Sub-Saharan African Travel
entities.description: Travel to or residence in rural endemic foci across 36 sub-Saharan African countries harboring competent tsetse fly populations.

entities.name: Endemic Latin America
entities.description: Travel, birth, or long-term residence in 21 continental Latin American nations where domestic triatomine cycles are established.

entities.name: Infected Blood Transfusion
entities.description: Iatrogenic parenteral exposure through transfusion of unscreened blood or platelet components harvested from asymptomatic parasitemic donors.

entities.name: Solid Organ Transplantation
entities.description: Transplantation of solid organs (kidney, liver, heart) from an infected donor to an uninfected recipient, or post-transplant immunosuppressive disease reactivation.

entities.name: Congenital Transplacental Route
entities.description: Vertical transplacental transmission of maternal trypomastigotes across the chorionic villi to the developing fetus during pregnancy.

entities.name: East African Safari
entities.description: Recreational safari tourism, wilderness game tracking, or travel to national parks in East and Southern Africa (e.g., Tanzania, Kenya, Malawi, Zambia).

entities.name: Agricultural Field Labor
entities.description: Occupational outdoor work including farming, hunting, fishing, cattle husbandry, and wood gathering in tsetse- or triatomine-infested environments.

entities.name: Marsupial Opossum Reservoirs
entities.description: Wild mammalian reservoirs, particularly the white-eared opossum (Didelphis marsupialis), maintaining high sylvatic parasitemia and anal gland parasite shedding.

entities.name: Wild Ungulate Reservoirs
entities.description: Wild African game ungulates including bushbuck, hartebeest, warthog, and waterbuck acting as natural sylvatic reservoir hosts for T. b. rhodesiense.

entities.name: Domestic Cattle Reservoirs
entities.description: Domestic zebu cattle and livestock in sub-Saharan Africa serving as primary domestic reservoirs for T. b. rhodesiense and suffering from nagana.

entities.name: Immunosuppressed HIV Patients
entities.description: Individuals with advanced HIV disease and CD4 counts < 200/mcL who experience catastrophic acute parasitic reactivation.

entities.name: Seropositive Pregnant Mothers
entities.description: Women of reproductive age chronically infected with T. cruzi who transmit the parasite vertically to their offspring in ~5% of pregnancies.

entities.name: Short Chagas Incubation
entities.description: Rapid incubation interval of 1 to 2 weeks following vector inoculation, or 3 to 22 days following oral ingestion of contaminated food.

entities.name: Prolonged Chagas Latency
entities.description: Extended clinical latency period spanning 10 to 30 years following primary infection before chronic cardiomyopathy or megadisease becomes clinically apparent.

entities.name: Acute Rhodesiense Incubation
entities.description: Brief incubation period of 1 to 3 weeks between infected tsetse fly bite and fulminant systemic symptom onset in East African sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Chronic Gambiense Incubation
entities.description: Indolent incubation period spanning several months to multiple years between tsetse bite and obvious clinical manifestations in West African sleeping sickness.

entities.name: Laboratory Needle Inoculation
entities.description: Accidental parenteral puncture or mucosal splash with viable trypomastigotes occurring in laboratory researchers and biomedical technicians.

entities.name: Zero Endemic Travel
entities.description: Complete lifelong lack of travel, residence, birth, or maternal origin in sub-Saharan Africa or Latin America, essentially excluding vector-acquired infection.

entities.name: Dual Negative Serology
entities.description: Concordantly non-reactive, negative results on two independent, validated serological assays detecting anti-T. cruzi IgG antibodies.

entities.name: Normal Electrocardiogram
entities.description: Completely normal standard 12-lead ECG demonstrating normal PR interval, normal QRS duration, normal axis, and absence of bundle branch blocks or ectopy.

entities.name: Normal Transthoracic Echocardiogram
entities.description: Echocardiogram showing normal chamber dimensions, preserved biventricular systolic function, and completely normal apical wall motion without aneurysm.

entities.name: Normal CSF Cellularity
entities.description: Cerebrospinal fluid examination showing white blood cell count < 5 cells per microliter and complete absence of trypanosomes.

entities.name: Absent CSF Mott Cells
entities.description: Total absence of morular plasma cells (Mott cells) and normal intrathecal IgM concentrations on cytocentrifuged CSF evaluation.

entities.name: Normal Esophageal Manometry
entities.description: High-resolution esophageal manometry showing normal coordinated peristalsis and complete lower esophageal sphincter relaxation upon deglutition.

entities.name: Normal Barium Enema
entities.description: Fluoroscopic contrast colon examination demonstrating normal colonic diameter, normal sigmoid length, and normal mucosal relief.

entities.name: Negative Blood Smears
entities.description: Repeatedly negative thick and thin Giemsa-stained blood smears and negative microhematocrit tube examinations during acute febrile illness.

entities.name: Absent Posterior Adenopathy
entities.description: Complete absence of posterior cervical lymphadenopathy (Winterbottom sign) upon careful neck palpation in a symptomatic West African patient.

entities.name: Preserved Normal Sleep
entities.description: Normal 24-hour sleep architecture without daytime hypersomnia, sleep attacks, or nocturnal wakefulness on clinical observation and polysomnography.

entities.name: Normal Card Agglutination
entities.description: Non-reactive CATT test in undiluted whole blood and serum, indicating absence of antibodies to T. b. gambiense.

entities.name: Negative Parasite PCR
entities.description: Negative molecular amplification of Trypanosoma cruzi kinetoplast DNA (kDNA) or satellite DNA in blood during acute or congenital presentation.

entities.name: Absent Apical Thinning
entities.description: Preserved left ventricular apical myocardial thickness and normal apical contractility without dyskinesia on contrast echocardiography or cardiac MRI.

entities.name: Normal Holter Telemetry
entities.description: Normal 24-hour ambulatory ECG recording demonstrating normal sinus rhythm without ventricular ectopic beats, non-sustained VT, or pauses.

entities.name: Normal Right Ventricle
entities.description: Normal right ventricular size, fractional area change (> 35%), and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE > 17 mm) on echocardiogram.

entities.name: Absence of Fecaloma
entities.description: Absence of palpable pelvic fecal masses, empty rectal vault on digital examination, and regular spontaneous bowel movements.

entities.name: Negative Node Aspirate
entities.description: Absence of motile hemoflagellates on fresh saline wet mount microscopy of aspirated posterior cervical node fluid.

entities.name: Normal Serum IgM
entities.description: Normal quantitative serum immunoglobulin M level without polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia.

entities.name: Absent Inoculation Lesions
entities.description: Complete absence of inoculation chagoma, Romaña sign, or trypanosomal chancre at insect bite locations in an acutely febrile traveler.

entities.name: Normal Myocardial Perfusion
entities.description: Normal myocardial perfusion SPECT or stress perfusion cardiac MRI without resting perfusion defects or scar in the left ventricular apex.

entities.name: Rapid Antibiotic Defervescence
entities.description: Prompt, complete resolution of fever and systemic symptoms within 24 to 48 hours of starting standard broad-spectrum antibacterial therapy.

entities.name: Cerebral Malaria
entities.description: Life-threatening Plasmodium falciparum complication presenting with acute encephalopathy, coma, and microvascular sequestration.

entities.name: Viral Encephalitis
entities.description: Acute viral inflammation of brain parenchyma (e.g., Herpes simplex, arboviruses) presenting with fever, focal seizures, and temporal lobe lesions.

entities.name: Dilated Cardiomyopathy
entities.description: Non-ischemic, idiopathic dilated myocardial failure featuring global biventricular hypokinesia and systolic failure without specific apical aneurysms.

entities.name: Ischemic Heart Disease
entities.description: Coronary artery atherosclerosis leading to myocardial ischemia, infarction, and regional wall motion abnormalities restricted to coronary vascular beds.

entities.name: Idiopathic Achalasia
entities.description: Primary esophageal motility disorder characterized by aperistalsis and impaired lower esophageal sphincter relaxation without known secondary infectious trigger.

entities.name: Hirschsprung Disease
entities.description: Congenital megacolon caused by failure of neural crest cells to migrate into the distal rectosigmoid during embryonic development, presenting in neonates.

entities.name: Visceral Leishmaniasis
entities.description: Disseminated protozoan infection caused by Leishmania donovani complex, presenting with pentad of fever, massive splenomegaly, pancytopenia, and wasting.

entities.name: Toxoplasma Encephalitis
entities.description: Opportunistic intracranial protozoan infection in immunocompromised hosts producing focal necrotizing brain abscesses in the basal ganglia.

entities.name: African Tick Bite Fever
entities.description: Rickettsial zoonosis caused by Rickettsia africae following tick bites in sub-Saharan savannahs, presenting with fever, inoculation eschars, and regional lymphadenitis.

entities.name: Tuberculous Meningitis
entities.description: Subacute granulomatous leptomeningitis caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, presenting with cranial neuropathies, basal meningeal enhancement, and low CSF glucose.

entities.name: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
entities.description: Progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by combined upper and lower motor neuron degeneration without sensory involvement or fever.

entities.name: Parkinson Disease
entities.description: Idiopathic neurodegenerative movement disorder characterized by resting pill-rolling tremor, lead-pipe rigidity, bradykinesia, and postural instability.

entities.name: Typhoid Fever
entities.description: Systemic bacteremia caused by Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi, manifesting with step-ladder fevers, relative bradycardia (Faget sign), and abdominal pain.

entities.name: Infective Endocarditis
entities.description: Microbial colonization of cardiac endocardium and heart valves producing oscillating vegetations, valvular destruction, systemic emboli, and positive blood cultures.

entities.name: Toxic Megacolon

relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis in its African form initially presents as the hemolymphatic first stage, characterized by extracellular parasite multiplication within subcutaneous tissues, peripheral circulation, and the lymphatic system.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis progresses to the meningoencephalitic second stage when trypanosomes cross the blood-brain barrier, triggering progressive neuroinflammation, severe cognitive deficits, and disrupted circadian rhythms.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis in Latin America manifests as acute Chagas disease within weeks of inoculation, characterized by high peripheral parasitemia, reticuloendothelial inflammation, and occasionally life-threatening acute myocarditis.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis enters the indeterminate chronic Chagas phase in approximately 60% to 70% of infected individuals, where patients remain asymptomatic for decades with normal ECG and imaging despite persistent latent parasitism.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy, featuring extensive myocardial fibrosis, biventricular enlargement, apical aneurysm formation, and refractory congestive heart failure.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as Chagasic megaesophagus due to denervation of the esophageal myenteric plexus, leading to aperistalsis, lower esophageal sphincter achalasia, and progressive dilation.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as Chagasic megacolon through progressive loss of colonic enteric neurons, resulting in colonic hypomotility, massive dilatation, and severe obstipation.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as the cardiodigestive form in up to 10% of chronic patients who experience concurrent fibrotic myocardial failure and gastrointestinal megadisease.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as circadian sleep fragmentation, where hypothalamic and suprachiasmatic nucleus neuroinflammation distorts endogenous circadian rhythmicity.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as progressive daytime somnolence, where patients experience irresistible daytime sleep attacks even while eating or conversing.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as nocturnal insomnia, with patients experiencing nocturnal agitation and inability to initiate or maintain sleep at night.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as acute trypanosomal myocarditis during primary infection, characterized by myocyte necrosis, diffuse inflammatory infiltrates, and sinus tachycardia.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as biventricular systolic failure, causing severe pulmonary congestion, elevated central venous pressure, hepatomegaly, and peripheral anasarca.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as cardioembolic stroke, triggered by the detachment of mural thrombi formed within an apical aneurysm, presenting with acute focal neurological deficits.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical presentation, sudden cardiac death
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as sudden cardiac death, representing the most common terminal event in chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy due to ventricular fibrillation or asystole.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as malignant ventricular arrhythmias arising from re-entrant circuits around patchy myocardial fibrotic scars in the ventricular walls.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as conduction system destruction, leading to complete atrioventricular dissociation, severe bradycardia, Adams-Stokes syncopal attacks, and pacemaker dependency.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as progressive neuropsychiatric decay in Stage 2 HAT, evolving from mild personality alterations to severe apathy, psychotic episodes, and profound dementia.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as a terminal comatose state in late Stage 2 sleeping sickness, characterized by total unresponsiveness, sphincter incontinence, and terminal inanition.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as extrapyramidal movement disorders in Stage 2 HAT due to parasitic basal ganglia and cerebellar peduncle inflammation.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as intractable esophageal dysphagia, causing patients to experience food impaction, retrosternal fullness, and an inability to swallow solid meals.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as severe odynophagia when fermenting food stagnant in the dilated esophagus induces mucosal erosion and painful secondary ulceration.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as nocturnal food regurgitation, where supine positioning causes retrograde emptying of stagnant esophageal contents into the pharynx.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as pulmonary aspiration syndrome, frequently presenting with chronic nocturnal coughing, choking episodes, recurrent bronchopneumonia, and bronchiectasis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as intractable chronic obstipation, with patients passing stools only once every few weeks due to complete loss of propulsive colonic motor activity.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as massive fecaloma impaction, producing rock-hard pelvic masses that require manual disimpaction, endoscopic fragmentation, or surgical extraction.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as acute sigmoid volvulus, a surgical emergency characterized by abrupt obstipation, severe abdominal colic, colonic ischemia, and gangrene.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as severe intestinal meteorism, causing dramatic visible abdominal swelling, diaphragm elevation, and exertional respiratory embarrassment.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as profound cachexia, leaving late-stage patients severely emaciated with loss of subcutaneous fat stores and profound muscle wasting.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as congenital trypanosomiasis in infected neonates, presenting with prematurity, respiratory distress syndrome, hydrops fetalis, and acute myocarditis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as Chagasic central reactivation in immunocompromised hosts, causing acute ring-enhancing intracranial mass lesions, seizures, and meningoencephalitis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as cutaneous chagoma formation at the vector bite site, featuring localized histiocytic infiltration, regional lymphangitis, and satellite adenopathy.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests via periorbital ocular inoculation, triggering inflammatory bipalpebral edema and conjunctival chemosis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as transient circinate erythema during Stage 1 HAT, presenting with non-pruritic, evanescent ring-like erythematous plaques on the chest and back.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as intermittent fevers, characterized by undulating febrile bouts that correspond to clonal expansion of variant surface glycoprotein trypanosome coats.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as debilitating pruritus in Stage 1 sleeping sickness, causing intense excoriation, sleep disturbance, and secondary pyogenic skin infections.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as severe throbbing headache, unresponsive to simple analgesics and reflecting intense systemic cytokine release and intracranial hypertension.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as disabling arthralgia during Stage 1 HAT, affecting major weight-bearing joints and limiting physical ambulation.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as pericardial effusion, which can progress from asymptomatic serous collection to hemodynamic cardiac tamponade during severe acute myocarditis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Trypanosomiasis manifests as fulminant Rhodesiense illness, featuring heavy parasitemia, rapid multi-organ failure, acute pancarditis, and death before classical Stage 2 signs emerge.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Trypanosomiasis features Winterbottom sign as a pathognomonic physical hallmark, presenting as painless, rubbery, mobile lymphadenopathy in the posterior cervical triangle.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Trypanosomiasis features Romaña sign as a pathognomonic hallmark, characterized by unilateral violaceous palpebral edema, conjunctivitis, and non-tender preauricular adenopathy.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Trypanosomiasis features the trypanosomal chancre as a pathognomonic inoculation hallmark, appearing within days of an infected tsetse fly bite as an inflammatory ulcerating furuncle.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Trypanosomiasis features the inoculation chagoma as a pathognomonic physical finding, marking the cutaneous portal of entry with hard, brawny inflammatory skin swelling.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Trypanosomiasis features circadian sleep reversal as a pathognomonic physical hallmark of Stage 2 HAT, with profound daytime somnolence and nocturnal motor insomnia.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Trypanosomiasis features the Kerandel hyperesthesia sign as a pathognomonic neuro-sensory hallmark, where light manual pressure over soft tissue elicits excruciating delayed pain.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical examination, posterior cervical adenopathy

[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits tender hepatomegaly on physical examination, occurring in acute chagasic myocarditis and during right-sided congestive heart failure.
[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits generalized lymphadenopathy during the acute hemolymphatic phase of infection across multiple peripheral nodal stations.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical examination, third heart sound

[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits a holosystolic murmur on auscultation due to progressive annular dilation and papillary muscle displacement in dilated cardiomyopathy.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical examination, jugular venous distension
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits jugular venous distension on cardiovascular examination, indicating severe right ventricular decompensation and systemic venous congestion.
[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits dependent peripheral edema on extremity examination, progressing upward to the thighs and sacrum in biventricular Chagas cardiomyopathy.
[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits resting tachycardia on physical examination, reflecting loss of inhibitory vagal parasympathetic tone from intracardiac ganglion destruction.
[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits choreiform motor incoordination on neurological exam in Stage 2 HAT, resulting from basal ganglia neuroinflammation.
[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits a postural intention tremor on physical assessment in meningoencephalitic sleeping sickness, impairing handwriting and fine motor skills.
[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits Parkinsonian cogwheel rigidity on tone assessment in advanced sleeping sickness, accompanied by hypokinesia and mask-like facies.
[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits cerebellar sensory ataxia on gait testing in Stage 2 sleeping sickness, rendering patients unable to walk in a tandem line.
[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits facial muscle grimacing on cranial nerve inspection, characterized by stereotyped lip-smacking, chewing, and involuntary facial grimaces.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical examination, apathy and mutism
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits apathy and mutism on mental status examination, progressing from social withdrawal to complete akinetic mutism.
[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits prominent abdominal distension on physical examination, often accompanied by visible bowel peristaltic waves and marked meteorism.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical examination, fecal impaction mass
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits a palpable fecal impaction mass on bimanual abdominal palpation in megacolon, confirming severe intraluminal stool retention.
[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits sluggish pupillary reflexes on neuro-ophthalmic examination, reflecting peripheral ciliary parasympathetic ganglion destruction.
[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits a transient circinate rash on dermatologic inspection, visible particularly in light-skinned patients during febrile waves of Stage 1 HAT.
[PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits pitting facial edema on physical inspection in acute childhood Chagas disease, often accompanying systemic fever and lymphadenopathy.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits motile extracellular trypomastigotes on fresh blood wet mount microscopy, confirming acute patent parasitemia at triage.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits Giemsa blood smear positivity, revealing classic C-shaped or S-shaped extracellular hemoflagellates under oil immersion microscopy.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits microhematocrit tube centrifugation concentration sensitivity, allowing rapid bedside detection of low-level acute parasitemia.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits lymph node aspirate positivity, where needle aspiration of enlarged Winterbottom nodes reveals active motile trypanosomes.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis (> 5 WBC/mcL) on diagnostic lumbar puncture, confirming meningoencephalitic CNS involvement in sleeping sickness.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits CSF Mott cells on cytocentrifuged cerebrospinal fluid analysis, serving as an indelible cytologic anchor of Stage 2 African sleeping sickness.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits CSF trypanosome identification upon microscopic review of centrifuged spinal fluid, establishing unequivocal diagnosis of Stage 2 HAT.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission laboratory, elevated csf protein
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits elevated CSF protein (> 45 mg/dL) on spinal fluid biochemical profiling, reflecting severe neuroinflammatory disruption.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits dual concordant serology positivity (e.g., ELISA and IFA) as the gold standard confirmation for chronic Chagas disease.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission laboratory, anti-t cruzi elisa
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits anti-Trypanosoma cruzi ELISA reactivity with elevated optical density ratios indicating chronic latent or symptomatic infection.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission laboratory, card agglutination test
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits card agglutination test (CATT) reactivity on field blood screening, identifying individuals infected with T. b. gambiense.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia on serum protein electrophoresis, with IgM concentrations frequently reaching 4 to 10 times normal values.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits moderate peripheral thrombocytopenia on admission complete blood count during acute Chagas and first-stage sleeping sickness.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits normocytic normochromic anemia on initial hematologic workup, compounded by dyserythropoiesis and hypersplenic sequestration.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits elevated erythrocyte sedimentation and acute-phase reactants during active hemolymphatic and acute myocarditic phases.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits mild transaminitis on admission hepatic panel testing during acute infection or hepatic congestion secondary to heart failure.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission laboratory, right bundle branch block
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits Right Bundle Branch Block on 12-lead ECG in over 40% to 50% of chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy patients, serving as its primary conduction hallmark.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission laboratory, left anterior fascicular block
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits Left Anterior Fascicular Block on ECG, reflecting preferential fibrotic damage to the anterior division of the left bundle branch.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits bifascicular conduction block (RBBB plus LAFB) on triage ECG, which possesses high predictive specificity for chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits high-degree AV block on electrocardiographic recording, manifesting with profound bradycardia and requiring permanent pacemaker implantation.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits ventricular ectopic complexes on admission rhythm strips, warning of impending malignant ventricular tachyarrhythmias.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits non-sustained ventricular tachycardia on ambulatory Holter monitoring, which stratifies patients at high risk for sudden cardiac death.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission laboratory, low qrs voltage
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Trypanosomiasis exhibits low QRS voltage on ECG profiling in advanced dilated cardiomyopathy, indicating extensive loss of viable contracting myocardium.

[IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits apical aneurysm on echocardiography, revealing a sharply demarcated, thin-walled outpouching at the left ventricular apex pathognomonic of chronic Chagas heart disease.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits left ventricular dilatation on echocardiography, displaying progressive cavity enlargement and global myocardial hypokinesia.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, diagnostic imaging, depressed ejection fraction
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits depressed ejection fraction on echocardiographic assessment, documenting severe systolic pump failure.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits intracardiac mural thrombus on apical echocardiographic views, identifying the anatomic nidus for systemic cardioembolic stroke.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits functional mitral regurgitation on color Doppler echocardiography, worsening backward left atrial pressure overload and pulmonary edema.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, diagnostic imaging, pericardial effusion ultrasound
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits pericardial effusion on bedside ultrasound, commonly seen in acute Chagas disease and acute rhodesiense sleeping sickness.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits cardiomegaly on chest radiography, demonstrating profound transverse cardiac enlargement from biventricular chamber dilatation.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits pulmonary venous congestion on chest X-ray in decompensated Chagas cardiomyopathy, demonstrating interstitial and alveolar pulmonary edema.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, diagnostic imaging, bird beak sign
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits the bird-beak esophageal sign on barium swallow, demonstrating distal pencil-tip tapering and severe luminal dilation mimicking idiopathic achalasia.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits esophageal luminal dilatation on contrast esophagography, showing aperistaltic contrast pooling, tertiary contractions, and delayed emptying.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits dolichomegacolon on barium enema, revealing massive colonic distension and an elongated sigmoid loop extending high into the upper abdomen.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits a colonic fecaloma mass on plain abdominal X-ray, seen as a large calcified or mottled stool mass distending the pelvic bowel lumen.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, diagnostic imaging, coffee bean sign
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits the sigmoid coffee-bean sign on abdominal radiograph in cases complicated by acute sigmoid volvulus, diagnosing acute closed-loop obstruction.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, diagnostic imaging, late gadolinium enhancement
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI, mapping extensive myocardial replacement fibrosis located preferentially in the apex and inferolateral wall.
[IMAGING_FINDING] Trypanosomiasis exhibits cerebral ring-enhancing lesions on brain MRI in immunosuppressed patients with Chagas reactivation, mimicking intracranial toxoplasmosis or lymphoma.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis transmission occurs through triatomine bug inoculation, where nocturnal blood-sucking bugs defecate metacyclic trypomastigotes near the bite wound.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis transmission is strongly associated with residence in homes featuring cracked adobe walls and thatch roofs that harbor dense infestations of kissing bugs.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis transmission occurs through contaminated açaí juice or fresh sugarcane juice, triggering explosive micro-epidemics of acute Chagas myocarditis.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis transmission in West and Central Africa is mediated by the riverine tsetse fly (Glossina palpalis), transmitting anthroponotic T. b. gambiense.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis transmission in Eastern Africa occurs through the savannah tsetse fly (Glossina morsitans), transmitting virulent zoonotic T. b. rhodesiense.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis acquisition requires epidemiological exposure through sub-Saharan African travel or rural residence within well-defined geographical tsetse belts.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis requires epidemiologic exposure to endemic Latin America (e.g., Bolivia, Argentina, Brazil, Mexico) where rural poverty and vector habitats overlap.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis transmission occurs through infected blood transfusion, serving as a prominent mechanism of spread in non-endemic metropolitan urban centers.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis transmission is mediated by solid organ transplantation from seropositive donors, causing acute fulminant graft rejection or disseminated infection.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis transmission occurs via the congenital transplacental route, accounting for over 10,000 new neonatal Chagas infections annually worldwide.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, tourist exposure, east african safari
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis transmission frequently affects tourists during East African safari excursions where game-viewing open vehicles attract savannah tsetse flies.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis exposure is heavily concentrated among rural populations performing agricultural field labor near river crossings, coffee plantations, or animal corrals.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Trypanosomiasis is maintained by marsupial opossum reservoirs (Didelphis), which bridge the sylvatic and domestic transmission cycles near human habitations.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Trypanosomiasis in East Africa relies on wild ungulate reservoirs that remain asymptomatic carriers of human-pathogenic T. b. rhodesiense.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Trypanosomiasis transmission is amplified by domestic cattle reservoirs in East Africa, which sustain high tsetse fly infection rates in pastoral communities.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, high risk host, hiv coinfection
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Trypanosomiasis exhibits high-risk vulnerability in immunosuppressed HIV patients, leading to acute pseudotumoral brain abscesses and fulminant myocarditis.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, high risk host, pregnant mothers
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Trypanosomiasis transmission centers on seropositive pregnant mothers, necessitating systematic maternal screening in both endemic and non-endemic countries.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, incubation period, acute chagas incubation
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Trypanosomiasis has a short Chagas incubation period of 1 to 2 weeks after triatomine bite inoculation, or as brief as 3 days following oral contaminated juice ingestion.
[INCUBATION_PERIOD] Trypanosomiasis is characterized by prolonged Chagas latency, remaining clinically silent in the indeterminate stage for 10 to 30 years before organ damage emerges.
[INCUBATION_PERIOD] Trypanosomiasis caused by T. b. rhodesiense exhibits an acute Rhodesiense incubation period of 1 to 3 weeks, manifesting rapidly with fever and chancre.
[INCUBATION_PERIOD] Trypanosomiasis caused by T. b. gambiense features a chronic Gambiense incubation period extending months to years, allowing insidious progression to Stage 2 CNS disease.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, occupational exposure, laboratory needle stick
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Trypanosomiasis can be transmitted through laboratory needle inoculation, presenting acutely with an accelerated incubation period and local chancre formation.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis is ruled out by zero endemic travel or residence in Latin America or sub-Saharan Africa in patients without a history of blood transfusion or organ transplant.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis (chronic Chagas disease) is conclusively ruled out by dual negative serology on two separate high-sensitivity IgG tests using different parasite antigens.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis as the etiology of symptomatic heart failure is effectively ruled out by a completely normal electrocardiogram lacking RBBB, LAFB, or ventricular arrhythmias.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis (Chagas cardiomyopathy) is ruled out by a completely normal transthoracic echocardiogram demonstrating preserved ejection fraction and intact apical geometry.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis second-stage meningoencephalitis is ruled out by normal CSF cellularity (< 5 WBC/mcL) and absent trypanosomes on centrifuged CSF microscopy.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, absent mott cells
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis Stage 2 sleeping sickness is ruled out by absent CSF Mott cells and normal intrathecal immunoglobulin indices.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis as the cause of dysphagia is ruled out by normal esophageal manometry demonstrating normal peristaltic progression and lower esophageal sphincter relaxation.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, normal barium enema
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis as the cause of severe obstipation is ruled out by a normal barium enema showing normal rectosigmoid diameter and absence of colonic elongation.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative blood smears
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis in its acute phase is ruled out by serial negative blood smears and negative concentration tests during symptomatic febrile episodes.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis (Stage 1 T. b. gambiense) is made highly unlikely by absent posterior adenopathy (negative Winterbottom sign) in an exposed individual.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis (advanced Stage 2 sleeping sickness) is ruled out by preserved normal sleep rhythmicity and absence of circadian reversal.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis caused by T. b. gambiense is ruled out by a persistently normal card agglutination test (CATT non-reactive) during field screening.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis in suspected congenital or acute cases is ruled out by serial negative parasite PCR assays demonstrating absence of circulating parasite DNA.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, absent apical aneurysm
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis (Chagas cardiomyopathy) is ruled out by absent apical thinning or dyskinesia on high-resolution contrast-enhanced echocardiography.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis cardiomyopathy with arrhythmogenic risk is ruled out by normal Holter telemetry lacking premature ventricular contractions and conduction delays.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, normal right ventricle
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis in advanced cardiomyopathy is ruled out by a normal right ventricle without chamber dilation or systolic impairment.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis megacolon is ruled out by absence of fecaloma, normal rectal tone, and normal regular spontaneous defecation.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis (Stage 1 sleeping sickness) is ruled out by a negative node aspirate on repeated microscopic examinations of enlarged cervical nodes.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis (African sleeping sickness) is strongly excluded by normal serum IgM levels, as active HAT consistently produces profound IgM elevation.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, absent inoculation lesion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis suspicion is markedly reduced by absent inoculation lesions (no chancre or chagoma) in an acutely febrile returning safari traveler.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis cardiomyopathy is ruled out by normal myocardial perfusion imaging showing absence of microvascular hypoperfusion or regional apical scar.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Trypanosomiasis is ruled out by rapid antibiotic defervescence following beta-lactam or macrolide administration, confirming a pyogenic bacterial etiology.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from cerebral malaria because malaria presents with intraerythrocytic Plasmodium ring forms on blood smears, acute rapid coma without chronic sleep inversion, and responds rapidly to intravenous artesunate.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from viral encephalitis because viral encephalitis features acute rapid onset, focal seizures, temporal lobe MRI T2-hyperintensities, and negative trypanosomal serology and absence of CSF Mott cells.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy because Chagas cardiomyopathy features pathognomonic left ventricular apical aneurysm, bifascicular block (RBBB plus LAFB), positive T. cruzi serology, and associated digestive megasyndromes, whereas idiopathic DCM causes diffuse global hypokinesia without apical thinning.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, differential diagnosis, ischemic heart disease
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from ischemic heart disease because ischemic cardiomyopathy shows epicardial coronary artery stenoses on angiography, whereas Chagas cardiomyopathy typically presents with angiographically normal coronaries, localized apical thinning, and positive T. cruzi serology.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from idiopathic achalasia because Chagas megaesophagus is accompanied by positive anti-T. cruzi serology, concurrent apical cardiac aneurysms, bundle branch blocks on ECG, and an epidemiological history of rural Latin American residence.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from Hirschsprung disease because Hirschsprung disease is a congenital aganglionosis diagnosed in infancy with a narrow distal rectal segment, whereas Chagasic megacolon is an acquired adult neuropathy with uniform dilatation down to the anal sphincter and positive T. cruzi serology.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from visceral leishmaniasis because visceral leishmaniasis causes profound pancytopenia and intracellular amastigotes (LD bodies) within bone marrow macrophages, whereas trypanosomiasis features motile extracellular hemoflagellates, Winterbottom adenopathy, or Chagasic apical aneurysms.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from toxoplasma encephalitis in HIV patients because toxoplasmosis typically shows multiple basal ganglia lesions responsive to pyrimethamine-sulfadiazine, whereas Chagasic pseudotumoral mass lesions contain T. cruzi amastigotes, react to benznidazole, and show positive Chagas serology.

relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from African tick bite fever because R. africae produces multiple necrotic tick eschars with black crusts, prominent regional adenitis, vesicular exanthem, and responds promptly to doxycycline, whereas trypanosomal chancres harbor extracellular trypanosomes.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from tuberculous meningitis because tuberculous meningitis exhibits severe CSF hypoglycorrhachia (CSF glucose < 20 mg/dL), basal arachnoiditis on contrast MRI, and positive acid-fast bacilli or GeneXpert PCR, whereas Stage 2 HAT features normal or mildly depressed glucose, Mott cells, and trypanosomes.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis because ALS exhibits progressive motor neuron loss with normal CSF cellularity, preserved sleep-wake architecture, absent systemic signs, and no endemic travel exposure.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from Parkinson disease because Parkinson disease lacks systemic inflammatory features, exhibits no CSF pleocytosis or Mott cells, shows asymmetric resting tremor improving with dopaminergic therapy, and lacks travel history to tsetse belts.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from typhoid fever because typhoid fever features positive blood cultures for Gram-negative bacilli, leukopenia, and prompt therapeutic response to ceftriaxone or azithromycin, while lacking hemoflagellates and Winterbottom sign.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from infective endocarditis because endocarditis exhibits discrete mobile valvular vegetations on echocardiogram, positive bacterial blood cultures, and peripheral vascular stigmata, whereas Chagas cardiomyopathy presents with apical aneurysm, mural thrombus, and conduction blocks.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from toxic megacolon because toxic megacolon is an acute, hyperinflammatory, septic complication with leukocytosis, fever, and bloody diarrhea, whereas Chagasic megacolon is an indolent, afebrile, chronic neurogenic dilation with fecaloma impaction.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from hypothyroidism because hypothyroidism shows markedly elevated serum TSH and low free T4, reverses completely with levothyroxine replacement, and lacks anti-trypanosome antibodies or motile parasites.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Trypanosomiasis is differentiated from Epstein-Barr mononucleosis because EBV mononucleosis features acute exudative tonsillitis, atypical lymphocytosis (> 10%) on blood smear, positive heterophile Monospot test, and self-resolving tender lymphadenopathy without motile hemoflagellates.
